agent_notes: Scope: two hunks in triggarr/web/routes.py. One passes shutdown_drain_timeout into the GET /settings template context; the other parses it in POST /settings through the new safe_float helper (validation.py:203).
No public API change. safe_float is a new import, and none of the 17 importers of routes.py depend on save_settings's signature or the form schema.
Schema: this adds a TOML key, [general].shutdown_drain_timeout. It is backward compatible because GeneralConfig defaults it to 60.0. No migration is needed.

Input hardening: safe_float rejects non-numeric, NaN and inf (math.isfinite) and clamps to [1.0, 3600.0]. Pydantic also sets ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False, so no unbounded or non-finite value can reach disk through the UI. The tightening is sound.

Main risk (impact-1): no template under triggarr/templates has a shutdown_drain_timeout input, so every POST /settings from the real UI writes the 60.0 default. This overwrites any custom value set in config.toml. The fix is the template input or a fallback to the current value. Recent commits (ce567d3, 'add failing drain-timeout settings round-trip test') suggest the template is the next step of the TDD cycle.
Runtime effect (impact-3): scheduler.py:81 takes _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT from the TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env var at import, so the config field is not used at runtime yet.
Performance: none. Parsing one float per settings save is trivial.
Blast radius: limited to the Settings page save path and one config key. Worst case is a silently reset drain timeout, and today that changes nothing at runtime.
Verdict: no blocking issue on its own. Do not ship without the template input, because without it impact-1 overwrites file-configured values on every save.

Verified: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout (triggarr/models/config.py:139) has ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False as a second validation layer beneath the form's safe_float clamp, and save_settings wraps SettingsModel construction in try/except before writing (existing QUAL-02 pattern). No ORM objects or secrets touched -- context dict in TemplateResponse carries only a plain float. No findings in this diff.
The new setting is persisted but cannot be edited through the UI and does not control shutdown behavior.

findings.fix_hint: Read the current general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown, retaining the intended environment override, and test that saving 120.5 changes the effective drain timeout.
findings.problem: Posting shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now succeeds and persists that value, but scheduler.py:81 still initializes the drain timeout exclusively from the environment, and scheduler.py:634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown still times out after 60 seconds, regardless of the saved setting or a restart. Operators cannot obtain the longer drain period this endpoint now accepts.

findings.fix_hint: Add a numeric shutdown_drain_timeout input associated with settings-form, render the current value, and support fractional values with the same bounds as the handler. Preserve the current value when the field is omitted.
findings.problem: The added template context has no corresponding input in settings.html. Users cannot view or edit the timeout, and browser submissions omit it, causing the new save logic to write 60.0. Thus a value of 120.5 saved through a direct POST is reset by the next ordinary settings save. The existing rendering assertion in tests/test_web.py:694 also requires this missing field.
